proposal_reason:
ANALYSIS: No fusion trials yet. The single-model+meta baselines are close (0.863-0.870), and uni2h+meta is best at 0.870. All three tuned members prefer strong regularisation (C 1e-4 to 1e-3). Embeddings share tile-level attention, so the models' errors may be correlated.
REASONING: Start exploration with the simplest strong fusion: late_tuned with mean_prob. Each member runs at its own validated setting, and averaging probabilities is a low-variance combiner with nothing extra to learn. This shows whether the members are complementary enough to beat the best single model.
EXPECTED: Expect AUROC around 0.875-0.885, a modest gain over 0.870 from averaging. If it is at or below 0.870, the members are largely redundant (shared attention), and fusion gains must come from weighting or early fusion rather than averaging.

ANALYSIS: Late_tuned mean_prob gives 0.8768, about +0.007 over the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.8701), and has a lower fold SD (0.025). Averaging calibrated per-model probabilities seems to help modestly. Early, gated, early_tuned and late with shared settings are still untested.
REASONING: The exploration phase should map every method. Early fusion is the most basic alternative. The tuned members prefer strong regularisation (C 1e-4 to 1e-3) and no PCA, so early with C=0.001, no PCA, balance_blocks=true (so Virchow2's 2560 columns don't dominate) and L2 norm tests whether joint training beats averaging.
EXPECTED: Expect about 0.865-0.88. If it falls clearly below late_tuned, joint fitting overfits at n=134 and I will concentrate on late/late_tuned combiners. If it matches or exceeds late_tuned, the next trials will tune C and meta_weight for early.

ANALYSIS: Both fusions so far (late_tuned mean_prob 0.877, early balanced L2 C=0.001 0.878) beat the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870) by ~0.007-0.008, which is likely near the acceptance threshold. Per-class profiles are similar; Papillary (0.78) and Lepidic (0.82) are the weak classes. Gated, late (shared C), and early_tuned remain untested.
REASONING: Exploration should cover the untested methods. early_tuned keeps each member's tuned preprocessing and learns block weights by inner CV, which could down-weight weaker blocks. C=0.001 matches the scale that worked in trial #2 and in uni2h's baseline. meta_weight=3 matches trial #2. This makes it a direct comparison of tuned per-block preprocessing plus block weights against uniform balanced blocks.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.878-0.885. If it is at or below 0.875, then per-block tuning and weights add nothing over simple balanced early fusion. In that case I would focus on C and PCA within plain early fusion, and on gated and stack for diversity.

ANALYSIS: All three fusion families tried so far (late_tuned mean_prob, early L2+balanced at C=0.001, early_tuned) land at 0.877-0.880, about +0.007-0.010 over uni2h+meta (0.870). That margin is near the noise threshold. Gated, the late variants with a shared config, and the learned combiners (stack, learned_weights) are still untested.
REASONING: The exploration phase should map every method. Gated is the only family with a non-linear, per-patient model weighting, and it has not been tried. I will use a conservative setting to limit overfitting on 134 patients: PCA 32 per model, L2 norm, hidden 32, dropout 0.5, weight_decay 0.1, 200 epochs, lr 0.001, 3 seeds, meta_weight 3.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.86-0.88, likely with a higher fold SD than the linear fusions. If it falls clearly below 0.87, I will treat gated as too data-hungry here and drop it, and spend the remaining exploration on late stack/learned_weights and on the C/PCA settings for early fusion.

ANALYSIS: All fusion methods land near 0.87-0.88, a little above the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). The leader is early_tuned (0.8796), with early balanced L2 (0.8784) close behind. Gated is no better than the single models. Untested so far are plain late and the stack / learned_weights combiners.
REASONING: Use the exploration phase to map the methods not yet tried. late_tuned with stack, at a strong stack penalty (stack_C=0.01), checks whether a learned second-level combiner adds anything beyond mean_prob. It can reweight models per class, for example where Papillary and Lepidic are weak. The strong penalty limits overfitting with only 134 patients per fold.
EXPECTED: I expect roughly 0.875-0.885. If stack does not beat mean_prob (0.8768), learned combiners are adding noise at this sample size. In that case I would keep the simple averaging or early-style fusions as the main candidates.

ANALYSIS: Every linear fusion beats the best single model (uni2h+meta, 0.870) by roughly 0.007-0.010 AUROC. The best so far are early_tuned (0.8796) and early with L2, balanced blocks and C=0.001 (0.8784); simple mean_prob late fusion gives 0.8768. Stacking and gated fusion add complexity and do not help (about 0.869), which fits overfitting with only 134 training patients per fold. Papillary (0.78-0.79) and Lepidic (about 0.83) are the weak classes in every trial.
REASONING: Strong shrinkage (C around 0.001) suits these data. Untested parts of the space are the late method with a shared config, PCA in early fusion, and stronger regularisation. Early fusion with PCA 64 per model tests whether reducing dimension before concatenation helps. Each model then contributes comparable low-variance components, which could allow a weaker penalty and better use of the complementary signal. I keep L2 and balanced blocks from #2 and move C to 0.01, since PCA removes many columns.
EXPECTED: AUROC of about 0.875-0.885. If it falls below #2 (0.878), then PCA discards useful variance and the full-dimension, heavily shrunk ridge setting is preferable. I would then explore around early_tuned with C and meta_weight instead.

ANALYSIS: Simple fusions (late_tuned mean_prob 0.8768, early L2 C=0.001 balanced 0.8784, early_tuned 0.8796) beat the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.8701) by about 0.008-0.01. That gain is likely near the acceptance threshold. Stacking (0.8686), gated (0.8694) and PCA64 with C=0.01 (0.8622) were worse, which suggests strong regularisation and simple combiners work best with 134 training patients. Papillary (~0.79) and Lepidic (~0.83) are the weakest classes for every method.
REASONING: The late method with a shared C has not been tested yet. Mean_logit on strongly regularised members (L2 on, no PCA, C=0.001) is a different combiner from mean_prob and answers whether late fusion with a shared, stronger-L2 setup can match early fusion. Using the exploration slot to map this method and combiner is more informative than another early_tuned C tweak.
EXPECTED: I expect about 0.875-0.880 AUROC, close to the early fusions. If it is clearly lower (<0.87), the shared C / L2 setting hurts the Virchow2 and H-optimus members, whose tuned baselines used no L2 and C=0.0001. In that case I would concentrate on early_tuned and early with C/meta_weight variations.

ANALYSIS: Fusion consistently reaches ~0.877-0.881, roughly 0.007-0.011 above the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). Strong regularization (C=0.001, no PCA, L2 norm) works best. PCA at 64 with C=0.01 hurt, and stacking and gated were weaker. The top trial is late mean_logit with shared L2/C=0.001 (0.8808).
REASONING: Three exploration trials remain, so this one should map an untested axis: meta_weight. Trial #3 suggested metadata helps uni2h at meta_weight=10, but every fusion trial so far used 3. Testing early_tuned at meta_weight=10 with C=0.001 answers whether less metadata shrinkage adds signal. Metadata alone gives 0.60 AUROC, so it may add something beyond the images.
EXPECTED: I expect a small gain, about +0.003, from better metadata use. If AUROC is the same or lower, metadata weighting is saturated, and the remaining effort should go to C (0.0001) and combine rules in late fusion.

ANALYSIS: Linear fusions cluster at 0.877-0.881 AUROC, about 0.007-0.011 above the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). Late mean_logit with L2, C=0.001 and meta_weight 3 is the top trial so far (0.8808). Stacking, PCA64 at higher C, and gated all did worse, so heavier learning and more capacity hurt. Two parts of the space are still unexplored: the stronger-regularisation end (C=0.0001, which the virchow2 and hoptimus1 members preferred) and the learned_weights combiner.
REASONING: Late with learned_weights, keeping the best late settings (l2=True, C=0.001, meta_weight=3), tests whether inner-CV weighting beats equal averaging. Late fusion is the current leader, so this is the most informative exploration slot left. The remaining slot can then probe C.
EXPECTED: I expect roughly 0.875-0.882. If learned_weights does not beat mean_logit, equal weighting is sufficient: the models are roughly equally informative, and inner-CV weight estimation with only 134 patients per fold adds noise.

ANALYSIS: Simple fusions (late mean_logit 0.881, early_tuned 0.880, early L2 C=0.001 0.878) all beat the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870) by about 0.01. That gain is near the acceptance threshold. Stronger regularisation (C=0.001) with L2 helps. PCA64 with C=0.01 hurts, stacking hurts, and the gated network is no better than single models. Papillary (0.78) and Lepidic (0.83) are the weak classes.
REASONING: This is the last exploration slot, so it should map an untested but plausible direction. Late fusion with mean_logit and a shared C=0.0001 (stronger shrinkage, matching the tuned C for virchow2 and hoptimus1) checks whether more regularisation of the members helps the best method so far. It keeps L2 and meta_weight=3 fixed so that the comparison with #7 is clean.
EXPECTED: AUROC of about 0.88, possibly slightly higher if virchow2 and hoptimus1 benefit from stronger shrinkage. If it drops, C=0.001 is the right shared strength and later trials should vary meta_weight, early C=0.0001 or balance_blocks rather than C.
decision_reason: exploration phase: nothing is accepted; end of exploration: trial 7 (highest mean AUROC of the 10 explored trials) becomes the current best

proposal_reason:
ANALYSIS: Exploration shows fusion helps modestly: late mean_logit with L2, no PCA, meta 3, C=0.001 gives 0.8808 vs 0.8701 for the best single model (uni2h+meta). early_tuned and early with balanced blocks are close behind (0.877-0.880). PCA (#6), stacking (#5) and gated (#4) are worse. C=0.0001 underfits in late (0.8721). Papillary (0.78) and Lepidic (0.83) are the weakest classes in every method.
REASONING: The C axis for late is the biggest untested lever: 0.0001 was clearly worse than 0.001, but 0.01 is unknown. With L2-normalised, standardised features, slightly weaker regularisation per member may sharpen the logits, and mean_logit already averages out member variance. All other knobs stay as in #7, so the trial isolates C. Another combine rule at the same C would probably differ by less than the acceptance threshold.
EXPECTED: If AUROC rises to about 0.885 or more, C is under-tuned and I will next probe C=0.1. If it falls below 0.875, then C=0.001 is the optimum for late. In that case I would move to meta_weight=10 or to early_tuned at C=0.01 rather than pushing C further.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants cluster at 0.87-0.88, about +0.01 over the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). The best so far is late mean_logit with L2, no PCA, C=0.001, mw=3 (0.8808). C=0.001 is clearly the sweet spot (0.0001 and 0.01 are both worse). PCA hurt (#6), and stacking and gated underperform, consistent with overfitting at n=134 per fold.
REASONING: The main untested knob in the best late family is meta_weight. Metadata alone gives AUROC 0.60, and early_tuned preferred mw=3 over 10. Testing mw=1 in late mean_logit costs one trial and checks whether less metadata emphasis helps. A more promising alternative would be the late_tuned family with mean_logit, which has untested combines: it gives each member its own tuned C (0.0001 for virchow2 and hoptimus1). However, late at C=0.0001 was worse (#10) and late_tuned mean_prob scored 0.8768, so this route is unlikely to be clearly better. I will try late_tuned mean_logit instead of the mw knob, since it is cheap and the method is distinct.
EXPECTED: Likely within ±0.005 of #7, which is below the acceptance threshold. If it falls short, that confirms the fusion gains are saturating around 0.88. I would then test mw=1 or l2=false in late mean_logit before concluding that #7 is near the ceiling.

ANALYSIS: Fusion clusters at 0.876-0.881 AUROC, about +0.01 over the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). The best is late mean_logit with L2, no PCA, meta 3, C=0.001. Within late, C=0.001 beats both 0.0001 and 0.01, so C is near its optimum. PCA=64 hurt early fusion, stacking underperformed, and the gated network did not beat the linear methods. Remaining differences are mostly within noise (thresholds ~0.006).
REASONING: Untested knobs that could plausibly matter are meta_weight in late fusion (only 3 tried) and l2_normalize=False. The per-model baselines preferred no L2 for Virchow2 and H-optimus-1, but late_tuned (which uses those settings) did slightly worse, so L2 seems fine. Metadata alone gives AUROC 0.60, and with uni2h it preferred meta_weight=10. In early_tuned, meta 10 was slightly worse than meta 3, so meta 1 in late is a cleaner open question. A milder PCA=128 could also denoise. I'll test meta_weight=1 first, as the cheapest structural question.
EXPECTED: Likely about the same (0.875-0.882). If it is lower, metadata up-weighting helps and meta 3 stays. If it is not clearly better, metadata weighting is settled and I will move to PCA=128 or l2_normalize=False within late mean_logit.

ANALYSIS: All reasonable fusions cluster at 0.876-0.881, roughly +0.01 over the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). Late mean_logit with L2 and C=0.001 is best. C is clearly peaked at 0.001, meta_weight barely matters, PCA hurts, stacking hurts and gated underperforms. Papillary (~0.78) and Lepidic/Acinar (~0.84) remain the weak classes.
REASONING: One structurally different, untested lever on the late path is l2_normalize=False at C=0.001. Virchow2 and H-optimus tuned best without L2 (at C=1e-4), so removing L2 might shift per-member quality. mean_prob, weighted_vote and stack are lower-value next steps: mean_prob gave a similar result in late_tuned, weighted_vote loses calibration information, and stack hurt. Testing L2=False answers the remaining open preprocessing question cheaply.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC within ±0.005 of 0.881, most likely slightly lower, because the scale of unnormalized standardized features at C=0.001 differs from the setting the members preferred. If it fails, preprocessing is settled (L2, no PCA, C=0.001). The remaining budget would then go to a few high-variance probes, such as early_tuned at C=0.01 or gated with weight_decay=1.0, before accepting that about 0.88 is the ceiling.

ANALYSIS: Late fusion with a shared configuration (L2, C=0.001, meta_weight=3, mean_logit) is the accepted best at 0.8808, about 0.011 above the best single model, uni2h+meta at 0.8701. Neighbouring changes to C, meta_weight, L2, combine rule and the tuned variants all land within ±0.006 and are noise. Stacking and PCA=64 hurt, which points to overfitting with 134 patients per fold. Only one gated configuration has been tried, at 0.869.
REASONING: The linear late and early families look saturated around 0.878–0.881, so more local tuning there cannot clear the acceptance threshold. The main open question is whether the per-patient gate can add anything once it is strongly regularised. Trial #4 used moderate regularisation (weight_decay=0.1, hidden=32, 200 epochs). This trial pushes regularisation to the top of each range: weight_decay=1.0, hidden=16, dropout=0.5 and 100 epochs. It keeps PCA=32 and L2 normalisation so that only the regularisation changes.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC around 0.870–0.880. If it clearly beats #4 but not #7, the gated method was regularisation-limited but adds nothing over linear late fusion. If it is not above about 0.885, I will drop gated and take the space as saturated near 0.881. The remaining trials would then only probe the untested late combine rules (weighted_vote, mean_prob at C=0.001) before letting the stop rule end the search.

ANALYSIS: Fusion gives a consistent but modest lift over the best single model: about 0.877-0.881 versus 0.870 for uni2h+meta. The late mean_logit setting (C=0.001, L2, meta 3) is a flat optimum, since neighbouring C, meta_weight and L2 changes are all within noise. PCA (#6), stacking (#5) and gated (#4, #15) did not help. early_tuned at C=0.001 (0.8796) is close to the best.
REASONING: In early_tuned, a block weight w acts like a per-block inverse strength of C×w², and all weights are at most 1. At C=0.001, inner CV can therefore only shrink blocks further, toward 1.6e-5 to 6e-5 at weight 0.25. Raising C to 0.01 lets the inner CV choose a per-block strength from about 6e-4 to 0.01. That range brackets the tuned single-model settings: about 0.001 for uni2h and lower for virchow2 and hoptimus1. This is the one untested way to give each block a different regularisation strength inside a joint model. It is the most plausible route to a clear gain, rather than another local tweak of late mean_logit.
EXPECTED: If per-block strength matters, AUROC should reach about 0.885-0.89 and clear the roughly 0.005 threshold, with gains in Micropapillary and Papillary. If it lands at or below 0.88, joint-model block weighting adds nothing beyond simple late averaging. The fusion gain would then be saturated near 0.88, and I would spend the remaining trials on a few untested distinct options, such as weighted_vote or C=0.0001 without block balancing, before accepting #7.

ANALYSIS: Fusion gives a consistent gain of about 0.01 AUROC over the best single model. The best so far is late mean_logit with L2, C=0.001, meta_weight=3 (0.8808, #7). Small changes to C, meta_weight, L2, tuned members, gating and early_tuned have all been rejected or tied, so the late/early linear family around C=0.001 looks like a plateau. Low-dimensional PCA is still unexplored in late fusion. Its only test was early fusion with pca=64 at C=0.01 (#6), which confounded PCA with a weaker penalty.
REASONING: PCA to 32 components per model is a qualitatively different form of regularisation: it truncates to the dominant directions rather than shrinking all of them. That could help weak classes such as Papillary and Lepidic more than L2 shrinkage does. With only 32 standardised dimensions, a moderate C=0.01 is the appropriate strength. Keeping the best combiner (mean_logit, L2, meta_weight=3) isolates the effect of the dimensionality reduction. This is one of the few remaining knobs that could plausibly give a clear gain rather than a tiny one.
EXPECTED: Most likely AUROC between 0.870 and 0.885. A gain above the threshold (about 0.006 or more) would show that rank truncation beats ridge shrinkage here. If it is rejected or worse, I will conclude that PCA discards discriminative signal, stop exploring PCA, and test early fusion with balance_blocks=False or the remaining combiners (weighted_vote, stack) before accepting the plateau.

ANALYSIS: Fusion consistently reaches about 0.877-0.881, which is roughly +0.01 over the best single model (uni2h+meta, 0.870). Late mean_logit at C=0.001 with L2 normalisation (#7, 0.8808) is the best so far. In both late and early_tuned, moving C away from 0.001 toward weaker regularisation (0.01) hurt, and PCA hurt. Gated and stacking are no better, and the remaining late variants (meta_weight, L2) are within noise.
REASONING: Stronger regularisation is the one untested direction for early_tuned. The Virchow2 and H-optimus-1 members were tuned at C=1e-4, and the concatenated design has about 5.6k dimensions, so C=1e-4 with learned block weights (meta_weight=3, the better of the two tried) may suit the joint model better. Late at C=1e-4 dropped (#10), but early_tuned can rescale blocks, so the outcome is not implied. This also maps the left side of the C curve for early_tuned, where C=0.01 was clearly worse.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.875-0.885. I do not expect a clear gain over #7. If it falls below 0.877, then C=0.001 is the optimum for joint models and the fusion ceiling is about 0.88. In that case I would shift the remaining budget to a single robust check (e.g. late weighted_vote) rather than chasing noise.

ANALYSIS: Fusion has plateaued around 0.876–0.881 AUROC. All of the top configurations (late mean_logit, early, early_tuned) share L2 normalisation and C≈0.001, and beat the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870) by about 0.01. Changes to C, PCA, meta_weight, l2_normalize and the gated network all produced equal or worse results. Stacking and PCA consistently hurt. The early-fusion knob balance_blocks has only been tested set to True.
REASONING: With 7 trials left before the stop rule, the most useful step is to answer an open question in the strongest region of the space rather than tweak settings already shown to be flat. Without block balancing, Virchow2 (2560-d) dominates the concatenation by column count. This tests whether letting the larger block carry more weight changes early fusion, at the setting (L2, C=0.001, meta_weight 3) that worked best.
EXPECTED: Likely AUROC 0.872–0.880, probably slightly below #2 (0.8784), since Virchow2 alone is the weakest image model. If it exceeds #7 by more than the threshold, block weighting matters and is worth tuning. If not, I will conclude that early fusion is saturated, and spend the remaining trials on late weighted_vote or mean_prob before accepting #7.

ANALYSIS: All strong methods cluster at 0.876-0.881. Late mean_logit with shared C=0.001 and L2 is the best (0.8808). Changing C, PCA, meta_weight or L2 makes it equal or worse. early, early_tuned and late_tuned are within noise of it. Gated nets do not beat the linear fusions. The fusion gain over uni2h+meta (0.870) is about +0.01, and the plateau looks reached.
REASONING: The main untested combiner is weighted_vote on the best late base setting. stack was poor at stack_C=0.01 in late_tuned, but a stack with a weaker penalty (stack_C=0.1) on the best late base is also untested. Weighted_vote usually discards probability information, which hurts AUROC. So the stack is the more plausible way to get a clear gain: it can learn class-specific reweighting, which could help weak classes like Papillary and Lepidic. Inner-CV predictions on about 107 patients are noisy, though. I'll test late stack with stack_C=0.1 at C=0.001, L2, meta_weight 3.
EXPECTED: Most likely a result near or below 0.876, since stacking adds variance with this little data. A clear gain (>0.89) would show that class-specific combination matters. If it fails, I'll conclude the simple averaging fusion at about 0.881 is the ceiling and spend the remaining stop-rule trials on a few cheap checks rather than fine-tuning.

ANALYSIS: All reasonable linear fusions cluster at 0.876-0.881. That is about +0.01 over uni2h+meta (0.870), and every variant around #7 is rejected as noise. C=0.001 with L2 norm and no PCA is robustly best. PCA hurts, gated nets underperform, and metadata weight and block balancing barely matter. Five trials remain before the stop rule.
REASONING: Stacking with stack_C=0.1 gave the best BA (0.543) and the best Lepidic AUROC, so the open question is whether a less regularised stacker (stack_C=1.0) can pick up class-specific model weighting. That is the only plausible mechanism left for a clear gain. Fine local tweaks of C or meta cannot beat a threshold of about 0.005.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC around 0.875-0.882, likely rejected. If it is not clearly above 0.8808, I will conclude that the fusion ceiling is about 0.88 and that #7 (late mean_logit) is the final answer. The remaining trials should then not be spent chasing noise.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion lands at 0.870-0.881, a +0.01 gain over the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). The current best, late mean_logit with C=0.001, L2 and no PCA, sits on a flat plateau: changes to C, meta_weight, L2, stack, early vs early_tuned and gated all score the same or worse. PCA and larger C hurt consistently. Papillary (~0.78) and Lepidic (~0.83) are the weak classes for every method.
REASONING: Four trials remain before the stop rule, so the most useful step is to close open questions that could plausibly give a clear gain. Untested so far: weighted_vote, gated with a high hidden size and no PCA, and early with C=0.0001. Weighted_vote usually loses information compared with probability averaging, so it is unlikely to help. Gated without PCA but with strong regularisation is the one structurally different option left. The gated runs scored 0.869-0.872 with PCA=32, and PCA hurt the linear methods too, so PCA may be what limited them. I will try gated with pca=None, hidden=16, dropout=0.5, weight_decay=1.0, 100 epochs, l2_normalize true and meta_weight 3.
EXPECTED: Most likely AUROC around 0.875-0.88, which would be rejected. If it beats 0.89, then PCA was holding the gated method back and its neighbours deserve exploring. If it fails, that confirms the plateau, and late mean_logit stays the final fusion, about +0.01 over the best single model.

ANALYSIS: The fusion methods tried so far (late mean_logit, early, early_tuned, late_tuned, stack) all score about 0.876–0.881 AUROC, roughly +0.01 over the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). The current best is #7, late fusion with L2 norm, C=0.001 and mean_logit. Changes to C, PCA, meta_weight and L2 moved the score by at most about 0.002, or hurt it. Gated fusion and PCA consistently hurt. Per-class AUROC hardly varies between fusion methods; Papillary (~0.78) and Lepidic (~0.83) stay the weakest classes.
REASONING: Only 3 trials remain before the stop rule. Within late fusion at the best per-model setting, combine is the one knob not yet mapped for mean_prob and weighted_vote. Of these, mean_prob is the only one that could plausibly match or beat mean_logit on AUROC; vote-based combining discards the probability ranking that AUROC needs. In late_tuned, mean_prob scored slightly above mean_logit (0.8768 vs 0.8761). This trial cheaply tests whether arithmetic averaging helps the Micropapillary and Solid tails at the stronger shared C=0.001 setting.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.878–0.882, within noise of #7, so it will likely be rejected. If so, I conclude that the fusion plateau is around 0.88 and that the combination rule does not matter. I would then report #7 as the final fusion, a modest improvement of roughly +0.01 over uni2h+meta. A gain above the threshold (about 0.005) would be surprising and would deserve a check with a C=0.01 variant.

ANALYSIS: Fusion plateaus at ~0.878-0.881 AUROC (best #7 late mean_logit, L2, C=0.001, meta 3), about +0.01 over uni2h+meta. Changes to combine rule, meta_weight, L2, C and stacking all give gains within noise or losses. PCA and gated variants are consistently worse. The ceiling looks set by shared information across the three tile-fused embeddings, not by the fusion rule.
REASONING: Two trials remain before the stop rule. The one untested axis with any plausible upside is weighted_vote in plain late fusion. A cleaner question is whether early fusion with L2 and a smaller C (0.0001) and balanced blocks regularises the 5632-d concatenation better. #2 (C=0.001) scored 0.8784, and the early_tuned C=0.0001 run got good BA. But #10 showed that C=0.0001 hurt late fusion. weighted_vote is a hard-vote combiner and likely weaker for AUROC. So I choose early with C=0.0001: it is the remaining untested regularisation level for the concatenated model.
EXPECTED: Likely 0.872-0.880, i.e. no accepted gain. If it fails, I conclude fusion saturates around 0.88 and #7 stands as the final configuration. That is a modest (~+0.01) improvement over the best single model, and further search would only select on noise.

ANALYSIS: Fusion plateaus at about 0.878–0.881 AUROC. That is about 0.01 above the best single model (uni2h+meta, 0.870), and trial #7 has been accepted as the current best. Near trial #7, the shared-C late and early variants with L2 norm, no PCA and C between 0.0001 and 0.001 are statistically tied. PCA, larger C and gated networks all hurt, and stacking shifts balanced accuracy but not AUROC.
REASONING: This is the last trial before the stop rule fires.
